title: Air Starter Motor — Installation

issue.reason: Original issue of the air starter motor installation task.

abstract: Installation of the air starter motor on the accessory gearbox pad, with the pad seal fit, the dry motoring run and the residual speed record that closes the task on both starter standards.

sections.purpose: To install the air starter motor on the accessory gearbox pad and to prove the installation with a dry motoring run.
sections.job_setup_note: The fan cowl must be open and supported for the mechanical work. A pneumatic ground source and external power are needed for the dry motoring run, and the area behind the engine must be clear before it is started. The pad seal must be renewed at every installation. Two persons are needed.
sections.procedure: Make sure that the electrical power is removed and that the warning notices are in position. Remove the cap from the gearbox pad and clean the pad face. Examine the drive shaft splines and apply the approved spline grease sparingly. CAUTION: DO NOT OVERFILL THE SPLINE WITH GREASE. EXCESS GREASE IS THROWN INTO THE PAD SEAL AND CAUSES A LEAK THAT LOOKS LIKE A GEARBOX FAULT. Fit a new pad seal. Support the starter on the sling, align the splines by hand and push the unit squarely onto the pad. Install the pad bolts EN290030-3C and torque to 34 Nm in a diagonal sequence. Install the nozzle assembly HOL790179-18 at the air inlet and tighten the clamp PE187919-09 to 16 Nm. Connect the start valve electrical connector and lock it. Install the cranking shroud ASDE222426-98. Install the start valve clamp ZE172964-77. Restore the electrical power and connect the pneumatic ground source. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT THE AREA BEHIND THE ENGINE IS CLEAR AND THAT THE INTAKE IS CLEAR OF PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT BEFORE THE DRY MOTORING RUN. Do a dry motoring run and record the peak speed, the time to cut-out and the residual speed at the moment the starter disengages. Make sure that the recorded values are inside the acceptance table for the starter standard fitted.
sections.close_out: Disconnect the pneumatic ground source and remove the electrical power. Examine the pad area for oil leakage after the run. Make sure that no tools or hardware remain in the nacelle. Remove the hold-open rod and close the fan cowl. Remove the warning notices and the safety barriers. Record the installation, the serial number, the three motoring values and the starter standard fitted, which determines the duty cycle the crew may use.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The acceptance table differs between the delivered and the revised clutch standard, post MOD-111356.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the area behind the engine is clear before the dry motoring run.
Do not overfill the spline with grease.
Support the starter on the sling until the pad bolts are torqued.

title: Air Starter Motor — Installation

issue.reason: Shroud aperture named as the way to identify the fitted clutch standard on an installed engine, and the identification made part of the record.

abstract: Installation of the air starter motor on the accessory gearbox pad, with the pad seal fit, the standard identification read from the shroud aperture, the dry motoring run and the residual speed record.

sections.purpose: To install the air starter motor on the accessory gearbox pad and to prove the installation with a dry motoring run.
sections.job_setup_note: The fan cowl must be open and supported for the mechanical work. A pneumatic ground source and external power are needed for the dry motoring run, and the area behind the engine must be clear before it is started. The pad seal must be renewed at every installation. Establish which clutch standard the starter carries before it goes on: the two units are externally identical apart from the cranking shroud, which has a 40 mm witness aperture on the revised standard and a 15 mm one on the delivered standard. The shroud is the only way to read the standard on an installed engine, because the data plate faces the pad, and the answer decides both the acceptance table used here and the duty cycle the crew is entitled to. Two persons are needed.
sections.procedure: Make sure that the electrical power is removed and that the warning notices are in position. Remove the cap from the gearbox pad and clean the pad face. Examine the drive shaft splines and apply the approved spline grease sparingly. CAUTION: DO NOT OVERFILL THE SPLINE WITH GREASE. EXCESS GREASE IS THROWN INTO THE PAD SEAL AND CAUSES A LEAK THAT LOOKS LIKE A GEARBOX FAULT. Fit a new pad seal. Support the starter on the sling, align the splines by hand and push the unit squarely onto the pad. Install the pad bolts EN290030-3C and torque to 34 Nm in a diagonal sequence. Install the nozzle assembly HOL790179-18 at the air inlet and tighten the clamp PE187919-09 to 16 Nm. Connect the start valve electrical connector and lock it. Install the cranking shroud ASDE222426-98 supplied with the starter and do not exchange shrouds between units: the aperture size is what identifies the clutch standard once the unit is on the aircraft, and a shroud from the other standard makes the engine unreadable. Measure the aperture and record it, and confirm that the clutch witness mark can be read through the aperture where the larger aperture is fitted. Install the start valve clamp ZE172964-77. Restore the electrical power and connect the pneumatic ground source. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT THE AREA BEHIND THE ENGINE IS CLEAR AND THAT THE INTAKE IS CLEAR OF PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT BEFORE THE DRY MOTORING RUN. Do a dry motoring run and record the peak speed, the time to cut-out and the residual speed at the moment the starter disengages. Make sure that the recorded values are inside the acceptance table for the starter standard fitted.
sections.close_out: Disconnect the pneumatic ground source and remove the electrical power. Examine the pad area for oil leakage after the run. Make sure that no tools or hardware remain in the nacelle. Remove the hold-open rod and close the fan cowl. Remove the warning notices and the safety barriers. Record the installation, the serial number, the three motoring values, the shroud aperture measured and the starter standard it identifies. Where the two engines are found to be at different standards, say so in the record: the aircraft is then limited to the earlier duty cycle and the crew has to be told.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The acceptance table differs between the delivered and the revised clutch standard, post MOD-111356.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the area behind the engine is clear before the dry motoring run.
Do not overfill the spline with grease.
Support the starter on the sling until the pad bolts are torqued.
